snippet.title: WILD ETOSHA | Why a Lion Walked Away From the Easiest Meal of Her Life | Wildlife Documentary
snippet.description:
WILD ETOSHA | Why a Lion Walked Away From the Easiest Meal of Her Life | Wildlife Documentary

The queen of the dry plains. She brings down zebra, she outfights the hyena, she takes almost anything she wants. Almost anything. When the drought takes her prey and leaves her starving with two cubs to feed, she finds what looks like a gift: a nest of ostrich eggs, just sitting in the open grass. The easiest meal of her life. But that nest has a guardian — a bird with a kick that can break a lion's spine, and a mother that will not count the cost. Discover why the strongest hunter on the plains walked away from the easiest meal of her life — in this wildlife documentary.

Journey into Etosha National Park, Namibia, a land of dust and salt where the dry season decides who eats, through the eyes of Zalika, a lioness raising two cubs alone. She rules by one simple law: the strong take what they want. She drives a whole clan of hyenas off the nest with raw power — and for a moment, the eggs are hers. But then the ostrich returns, and it does not run. Witness the raw reality of survival, where the bird plants itself between the lion and its eggs, spreads its wings, and faces her down with two legs carrying a forward kick strong enough to kill. The strength that beat the hyenas is suddenly worthless. Because the egg is not guarded by a stronger animal — it is guarded by a price. One egg, against a kick that could leave her cubs motherless. And so the strongest hunter on the plains does the hardest thing a hunter can do: she walks away. This is the story of a queen who learned that power is not the same as getting everything — and that the wisest hunter is not the one who takes the most, but the one who knows what is not worth dying for.

An ostrich returning to its eggs — and charging the lion
The bird's forward kick, strong enough to break a lion's spine
The strongest hunter on the plains forced to back down
A queen choosing her cubs over the easiest meal of her life

Journey into Etosha National Park, Namibia, a land of dust and salt where the dry season decides who eats, through the eyes of Zalika, a lioness raising two cubs alone. She rules by one simple law: the strong take what they want. She drives a whole clan of hyenas off the nest with raw power — and for a moment, the eggs are hers. But then the ostrich returns, and it does not run. Witness the raw reality of survival, where the bird plants itself between the lion and its eggs, spreads its wings, and faces her down with two legs carrying a forward kick strong enough to kill. The strength that beat the hyenas is suddenly worthless. Because the egg is not guarded by a stronger animal — it is guarded by a price. One egg, against a kick that could leave her cubs motherless. And so the strongest hunter on the plains does the hardest thing a hunter can do: she walks away. This is the story of a queen who learned that power is not the same as getting everything — and that the wisest hunter is not the one who takes the most, but the one who knows what is not worth dying for.

snippet.title: The Pregnant King of the Mahabharata । Indraprastha
snippet.description:
The Pregnant King of the Mahabharata । Indraprastha 

History also mentions a pregnant king, whose story may leave you surprised.

The Mahabharata mentions King Yuvanashva of the Ikshvaku dynasty.

King Yuvanashva was a powerful ruler, and it is said that he performed the Ashvamedha Yajna several times.

But the biggest concern in his life was that he had no son.

Some Puranic traditions also mention that he had several wives, but despite this, he had no children.

The king was worried about who would succeed him and carry forward his dynasty and kingdom after his death.

So, one day, troubled by this concern, he went to the ashram of Sage Bhrigu.

The sages performed a special yajna for the king, and after the yajna, water was placed in a vessel.

It was believed that whichever queen drank this water would give birth to a son.

But King Yuvanashva had no idea about this.

Since the yajna was still going to continue for several days, the king stayed at the ashram.

One night, he became extremely thirsty. Seeing the water kept at the ashram, he drank it.

He had no idea that the water had been prepared for the queen.

According to the story, the effect of that water fell upon King Yuvanashva, and he himself became pregnant.

In other words, the Mahabharata describes the extraordinary story of a male king becoming pregnant in a miraculous manner.

When the time came for the child to be born, the birth did not take place in the usual way.

Now there was a problem: the child had no mother.

At that point, Lord Indra took responsibility for the child and raised him.

The child was named Mandhata, and he later became a very powerful king.

The Mahabharata says that he defeated many kings in battle and established a vast kingdom.

So, what do you think about this extraordinary story associated with King Yuvanashva and Mandhata?

snippet.title: The Last Castrato: A Voice That Shouldn’t Exist Today #history #italy #opera
snippet.description:
Alessandro Moreschi was one of the last famous castrati — male singers who underwent a procedure before puberty so they could preserve a high, childlike voice into adulthood.
At a time when women were banned from singing in many Catholic church choirs, castrati were used to perform the highest vocal parts.
This rare recording was made in 1902, when Moreschi was 44 years old, giving us one of the only surviving recordings of a real castrato voice.

snippet.title: One small act of kindness can become someone's whole new world. ❤
snippet.description:
Sometimes, the most beautiful stories begin with one person who simply refuses to look away. 🤍🐾
Late at night, while driving along a lonely road, @theherper spotted something tiny in the darkness.
A little kitten, all alone, with no one around to help him.
The area had been experiencing heavy storms, and the little one was dangerously close to passing traffic.
When the man stopped and approached, he heard the kitten's desperate little cries.
And he knew he couldn't just leave him there. ❤️
He carefully caught the frightened kitten, brought him into his car, and gave him something he desperately needed — safety.
But his kindness didn't end there.
Later that night, during a stop for food, he came across a group of young servicemen who were more than happy to take the little kitten into their care. 🥹❤️
And just like that, a tiny life that had been alone on a dark road was given the chance for a completely different future.
A future with people who would care for him. A future filled with hope.
All because one person chose to stop.
This is exactly what Tata Harmony Way is about — ordinary people with extraordinary hearts who understand that even the smallest life deserves a chance to be loved.
Because kindness isn't always just about saving someone from danger.
Sometimes, it's about making sure they have somewhere safe to go afterward.
Thank you, @theherper, for noticing this tiny life, choosing to help, and finding people willing to care for him. ❤

snippet.description:
Vielversprechende Ansätze und eine neue Goalgetterin: Die deutschen Fußballerinnen sind dank Doppelpackerin Melissa Kössler erfolgreich in die WM-Saison gestartet. Das Team von Bundestrainer Christian Wück bezwang Australien verdient mit 4:2 (2:1) und bestand den ersten Härtetest gegen ein außereuropäisches Topteam. 

Hier gibt es die Highlights der Bundesliga, der UEFA Champions League und des DFB-Pokals. Dazu die Highlights ausgewählter Partien der 2. Bundesliga und der Frauen-Bundesliga. Abonniere hier unseren Kanal: https://kurz.zdf.de/abosport/

208 Länderspiele, 126 Tore. Lionel Messi verabschiedet sich von der argentinischen Nationalmannschaft. Lange galt er in seiner Heimat als der Mann, der beim FC Barcelona alles gewann, im Trikot der Albiceleste aber nicht liefern konnte. Dann wurde aus dem tragischen Helden der Fußballgott einer ganzen Nation. Doch was bleibt von Messi, wenn der Größte geht? Der Bolzplatz blickt auf Messis schwierigen Weg zum Nationalhelden, sein einzigartiges Erbe und die Frage: Kann Argentinien auch ohne ihn erfolgreich sein? https://kurz.zdf.de/FrB/

ZDFsportstudio bei Instagram https://www.instagram.com/sportstudio/
ZDFsportstudio bei TikTok https://www.tiktok.com/@sportstudio.de
ZDFsportstudio bei WhatsApp https://kurz.zdf.de/6Em3U/

Vor allem Kössler (23., 30.) überzeugte gegen den WM-Vierten von 2023 mit ihren ersten Länderspieltoren, auch Camilla Küver (83.) erzielte ihren ersten Treffer für Deutschland. Auch die Defensive stand bis auf den Gegentreffer von Samantha Kerr (45.+1) und bei einigen Standardsituationen stabil. Der neuerliche Anschluss Australiens durch Holly McNamara (90.+2) trübte dann das Gesamtbild etwas. Dann stellte Sjoeke Nüsken (90.+4) nach einer weiteren Ecke den Zwei-Tore-Abstand wieder her.  

Die Aufstellungen:     

Deutschland: Mahmutovic – Wamser (69. Linder), Minge (89. Kleinherne), Küver, Kett (46. Müller) - Senß, Nüsken, Zicai (89. Freigang), Brand (46. Dallmann), Bühl (46. Baum) – Kössler (69. Anyomi)
